A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSGD research work. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Appendix H, Figures 1–2, reports original synthetic quadratic experiments measuring mean-squared error, empirical tail probabilities and network-size effects.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix H retain the synthetic experiments and add original nonconvex logistic-regression experiments on a9a, mushroom and ijcnn1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the adapt-then-combine DSGD update in Equation (3) remain unchanged. The new logistic-regression objective is an evaluation problem, while Appendix M extends analysis of the existing algorithm.

E1.justification: v4 evaluates only synthetic strongly convex quadratics. v6 retains these and adds nonconvex regularized logistic-regression optimization on three real datasets: a9a, mushroom and ijcnn1.

E2.justification: Both versions empirically evaluate DSGD without competing algorithms. Network sizes and thresholds are experimental configurations; comparisons with Lu et al. (2024) and centralized methods remain theoretical.

E3.justification: The added real-data protocol uses equal-sized agent partitions, fixed learning rate and regularization coefficient of 0.1, 1,000 iterations, and averaged squared-gradient norms. It includes 30-agent tail tests and 10/30/50-agent scaling tests. Appendix H retains the original synthetic settings.

E4.justification: v6 extends threshold sensitivity and controlled network-size analyses to real nonconvex problems, including scaling comparisons with connectivity held near lambda = 0.6. These extend the existing questions about tail decay and speed-up rather than introduce new component ablations.

E5.justification: The new real-data experiments report 100 runs and estimate tails across those runs. Synthetic run counts and Monte Carlo subsample counts remain unchanged. However, v6's main-text synthetic estimator averages over all R runs, conflicting with the retained subsampling description in Appendix H.1.

E6.justification: Figures 4–6 add gradient-norm and tail-probability curves reporting exponential tail decay on a9a/mushroom and faster convergence with larger networks on a9a/ijcnn1. The original synthetic findings, including approximately 6,000 iterations to reach mean error 0.0001, are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix M adds four lemmas and Theorem M.5 for step-size exponent eta in (1/2,1], stating a rate O(log(2d/delta)/(n t^(2eta-1)) + 1/t^(3eta-1)) in place of v4's informal O(1/(n t^eta)) discussion. v6 also revises the noise-tail derivation and initial-error terms in Appendices G/I, and removes the Polyak–Ruppert averaging bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the central claims: relaxed assumptions, order-optimal nonconvex and strongly convex HP rates, linear speed-up, and matching or sharper transient times. Added evidence does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v6 cautions that real-data minibatch noise need not satisfy the sub-Gaussian assumption and discusses stronger observed speed-up on the more heterogeneous a9a dataset. It removes v4's discussion of practical advantages of last iterates over Polyak–Ruppert averaging.

D1.justification: v6 documents the LIBSVM data source, nonconvex regularizer, agent allocation, hyperparameters and minibatch origin of randomness for the added experiments. Existing synthetic generation details remain. No code access, hardware or training-time information is added.

R1.justification: v6 adds Antoniadis et al. (2011) for nonquadratic penalties and Chang and Lin (2011) for LIBSVM, while removing the Ruppert and Polyak–Juditsky references with the averaging discussion. The main positioning against prior decentralized HP work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 adds a dedicated numerical-experiments section, subdivides Appendix H, adds acknowledgements and makes local wording, acronym and cross-reference edits. Most existing exposition and the overall narrative sequence remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from single to double columns, with extensive equation and appendix reformatting. Original Figures 1–2 become Figures 2–3; selected panels are reused in new Figure 1. Figures 4–6 add real-data displays, including zoomed insets.

improvement.justification: Real-data validation and the repaired noise-tail argument strengthen the paper. However, new Lemma M.2 drops necessary initial-condition scaling, and Appendix G's revised Equation (46) loses an n factor required by its unchanged process definition. Figure 4's caption also contradicts its threshold legends, and the synthetic estimator descriptions disagree. These empirical gains and mathematical/reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
